answer.rationale: Rated purely on how directly each claim evidences sustainable long-term qualified revenue, given what is written and what is omitted. memory_57 is strongest (5): it names qualified revenue explicitly and checks the durability side by reporting no measurable retention harm — it covers both halves of the objective. memory_44 is next (4): pipeline quality from enterprise sales-assisted flows is close to qualified revenue and implies durable, high-value accounts, though it stops at pipeline rather than closed or retained revenue and says nothing about cost-to-serve. memory_73 (3) reports actual acquisition and revenue lift, but promotional pricing revenue is the most suspect kind: nothing is said about margin, discount-cohort retention, or whether the lift persisted after the promo ended, so it may be pulled-forward rather than sustainable revenue. memory_86 (2) and memory_31 (2) are funnel-proxy findings — completion, time-to-value, activation — with no revenue or retention linkage; memory_31 at least claims a 'durable' lift, but durability is asserted only over the first week, which is not a long horizon. memory_91 is weakest (1): week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the shortest-horizon, most easily-moved proxies in the set, with no evidence of persistence beyond week one, no conversion linkage, and no revenue or retention measurement at all — an in-product nudge can lift these numbers without any downstream economic effect. A general caveat across the whole set: all six are archived summaries with no effect sizes, sample sizes, confidence intervals, or segment definitions, and the four funnel memories chain through proxies that were never validated against revenue, so none should be treated as settled for this objective. Note also that the three highest-rated memories (57, 44, 73) describe revenue mechanisms not directly aimed at the two declining funnel metrics in the current situation, so the ratings should not be read as an experiment recommendation on their own.
